engagement_title: Astrid Vellacourt founder brand kit: one look across nine session frames, a monogram recovered from a blind-debossed card, cut-outs that hold on the deep ground, the speaker and announcement canvases handed back editable, and a printed run of per-engagement speaker cards merged one-per-talk off her Feb-to-May season roster
vertical: Personal branding for a founder: the co-founder and managing director of a six-person industrial design studio, raising a seed round and speaking on a European conference circuit
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-20 (Freelancer.com, reference null). Its grounding_note, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Adapted from a real Freelancer.com creative-headshot brief (a founder wanting a creative and dynamic headshot for my professional business profile, shot in a studio with studio lighting and creative and dynamic compositions). The live studio shoot itself is out of connector scope, so the task is faithfully scoped to the POST-PRODUCTION + personal-brand delivery a creative-headshot retoucher hands over once the raw studio frames exist. The client is laundered to a FICTIONAL unnamed founder with a generic two-letter personal monogram (AV); no real person, company, product, platform or trademark is named.' Absorbs AO-21. The rebuild is needed because the ledger concept ended in a set of crops of one sitter, which is one deliverable rather than four, and sat on one surface. The fuller commission a founder on a raise actually buys is the one here: the session frames finished to one look, the cut-outs that have to hold on the deep ground her deck and press kit use, her monogram recovered from the only artefact that carries it, and the speaker and announcement canvases she edits herself between events. The founder is named Astrid Vellacourt, the studio is Vellacourt & Sund, and no real person, firm or platform is referenced.
client_one_liner: I got a mix of frames out of a half-day session and they do not match, my monogram only exists as a blind deboss on an old card, and I need one look that works everywhere from a tiny profile picture to a conference banner, plus a printed card for every talk I am giving, run off my own list so I am not laying out each one by hand.
client_brief:
I co-founded and run a six-person industrial design studio. We are raising a seed round and I am speaking at three conferences between February and May, so this is the season my picture is in front of people who do not know me yet.

I had a half-day session with a photographer and I have nine frames I like. They do not match. The light moved during the afternoon, some are warmer, one is much cooler than the rest, and put together they look like three different sittings. I want one look across all of them. Composed, credible, understated. I am asking people for money and asking conferences for stage time, so it should look like someone who runs a company, not someone who runs an account. No heavy filter, nothing that looks like a preset, and please do not smooth me into somebody else.

Here is what I actually need the pictures for. A profile picture, which is the smallest place any of this appears and where I care most. A press headshot I send to conference organisers. A wide banner for my profile pages. And a speaker photo for the programmes, which those organisers always ask for on a plain background so they can put it on their own colour.

That plain background is the thing I keep failing to solve myself. The session was shot on grey paper and I do not want grey. I want a warm neutral behind me. And for the press kit and my deck I need a version with nothing behind me at all, because both of those sit on a very dark ground and every version I have tried has a pale outline round my hair on it.

My monogram. When we started the studio we had cards made with the two letters pressed into the paper with no ink, just the impression. I love it and it is the only version that exists. I do not have a file and the printer that made them has closed. I want it back as artwork I can use, and it has to survive on a profile picture, which is where it is smallest, and reversed on the dark ground, which is where it is hardest.

The last piece is a speaker one-pager for the conferences, a wide banner canvas and a square announcement I post when a talk is confirmed. Those three in one file I can edit myself, because the event name and the date change every time and I am not paying for this four times.

One more thing. The banner wants something with more room than a studio frame, my studio or a workshop, and we have nothing usable. If that is what it needs, source one and bill me for it.

There is one printed thing on top of all that. For every talk I am giving I want a small card, one to a talk, with my picture on it, the talk title, the event and the date, and my monogram in the corner. They go in the delegate packs the conferences hand out and I give them to people I meet. My print shop set up one blank card for me and I have a list of every confirmed talk, panel and session between February and May with the event, the date, the title and which of my frames I want on each one. I am not laying out fifteen cards by hand and I really do not want the wrong date on the wrong card in front of an organiser, so build it so the whole run comes off my list and my print shop can print it.

What I need back: the nine finished, all four crops, the version on the warm neutral and the version with nothing behind me, my monogram as artwork with a note on where it will and will not hold, the three canvases as one editable file plus whatever it was built from, the printed run of speaker cards off my list with the right talk on each one, a board I can send my co-founder, and a note on what you did.
price_band_and_audience: Founder personal-brand package. The client is 30 to 50, raising a seed round at institutional level and pitching a European speaking circuit, and her audience is investors, conference programme committees and prospective senior hires. The band is load-bearing on every decision. At this level the look is composed, credible and understated: neutral warm ground, natural skin, restrained contrast, one consistent framing logic, and the monogram used quietly rather than as a badge. An over-filtered influencer treatment, high clarity, bright teeth and eyes, a strong colour cast, misprices her to exactly the people she is asking for money, and a stiff corporate flash-on-white treatment makes a design studio founder look like an accountant. The collateral follows the same rule: air, one photograph doing the work, type that does not shout. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every crop is dimensionally correct. The ledger records the base concept at 400 to 900 dollars; this fuller commission, with the mark recovery and the editable canvases, runs 900 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_session/ (9 frames, 5200px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Nine frames I like out of the half-day. Shot on grey paper in a studio. The light moved during the afternoon and they do not match." Seated and standing, three-quarter and straight on, no other people.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things she cannot see. First, she has thick curly hair and the studio grey sits close in value to it in the frames shot after the key light was moved, so the knockout on those frames returns an edge that is either cut hard into the curl or carries a soft pale rim of captured grey. On white and on the warm neutral both look perfectly clean, which is why every version she has tried looked fine until it went on her deck. Second, the frame she has already decided is the press headshot, the one she calls her favourite, is the coolest of the nine and the furthest from where the other eight can reasonably be brought, so bringing the set to one look and honouring her choice of hero pull against each other, and nothing in the frame announces this until the nine are laid out together after correction.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_deboss_card.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our original card. The two letters are pressed into the paper with no ink at all, just the impression. It is the only version of the monogram that exists and the printer has closed." A 4,000px phone frame of a white cotton card on a pale desk, shot under a window at a raking angle.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A blind deboss carries no ink and no colour, so the mark exists only as the shadow the raking light throws in the relief, and it exists only on the side the light came from. On the lit side the letterforms have almost no edge at all. What a selection returns is therefore a property of that one photograph's light rather than of the mark, and what the trace yields is a set of soft shadow shapes that read convincingly as the monogram at full canvas and break into fragments at the size a profile picture reproduces it. There is no option on the tracing step to tune this, so the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be known until the result is placed at its real delivered size.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_workshop_snap.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A phone picture of our workshop, if it is any use for the banner."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: 1,300px on the long edge, shot handheld under mixed daylight and fluorescent tubes, with the bench in front of the camera and nothing behind it. It cannot carry a wide banner at any usable width and its content offers no room for type, which is only apparent once a banner crop is actually attempted from it.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_placements.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The four placements she needs and the delivered sizes each one is used at, the description of the warm neutral she wants in plain language, and the note that the press kit and the deck both sit on a very dark ground.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_bio_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: Her speaker biography, the studio's one-line description, the three confirmed talk titles and the announcement wording she uses when a talk is confirmed.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_speakercard_template.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The flat card my print shop set up for the speaker cards, one talk to a card. I want a run of them off my roster, one per talk, so I am not laying each one out by hand." A single-record A6 portrait card on the warm neutral ground: a portrait well across the top, the talk title, the event and the date beneath it, and the AV monogram in the bottom corner.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the card looks like printed and how the file is set are two different things. The talk title, the event name and the date read as three tidy fields but are set as one continuous threaded story in a single frame, with the date sitting in the middle of that story, so a mapping read straight off the layout omits the date from every card and reports nothing wrong. The portrait area is the one real picture frame on the card and binds a photograph cleanly. The monogram in the corner is not a frame at all but flattened artwork baked into the supplied PDF at its own low resolution, so it cannot be bound per record and ships fuzzy on every card unless it is replaced with the recovered vector as a shared element. And the media box equals the trim with no bleed box present, so a press-ready-with-bleed run cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called, and none of this is visible in the printed sample.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_talks.csv (8 engagements)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "My speaking season. Every confirmed talk, panel and session between February and May, with the event, the date, the title and which of my frames goes on the card." One row per engagement, with a picture column pointing at the session frame each card's portrait comes from.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One engagement was confirmed last week and its picture cell is simply blank, which no header reveals and which the merge will not complain about. The dates are written in five different formats across the rows. Two of the rows are the same conference on the same day, a panel and a fireside, so they share an event name and even write that shared date two different ways, which means naming one card file per event collides and silently overwrites one with the other. And the picture cells point at the session masters, not at card-shaped crops, so a card portrait has to be cut to the card's own proportion for every row rather than reused from any of the four named placement crops.

acceptance_bar: The nine read as one sitting when laid out together, not as three, and no frame jumps against its neighbours.
She still looks like herself. No smoothing, no visible retouching signature, no preset look.
All four crops are delivered for the placements named, each composed for the size it is actually used at rather than cropped down from one master.
The version with nothing behind her holds its edge on the dark ground her press kit and deck use, with no pale outline in the hair and no hard-cut curl, checked on that ground and not on white.
The version on the warm neutral is a warm neutral and she reads cleanly against it at every delivered size.
No invented pixels anywhere. No delivered file is larger than its source, and the note lists every picture any tool resized or extended, and by how much.
The monogram is placeable artwork with no white box behind it, and the note says honestly where it holds and where it does not, including at profile-picture size and reversed on the dark ground.
If the monogram will not hold somewhere she asked for it, that is named in writing with what to use instead, not quietly shipped broken.
All three canvases sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, and she gets the self-contained source it was built from.
The words in that file are live text she can retype and the monogram in it is real vector artwork, not a picture of a layout.
Anything licensed sits with her own photography rather than reading as a stock picture behind her.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
The board carries the finished set with nothing silently missing from it.
The note says, per frame, what was applied, and names any frame that could not be brought to the set.

The speaker card run produces one card per engagement, page count equalling the roster's row count, each card carrying its own talk's title, event and date, with the date present on every card and not dropped.

Each speaker card's portrait is cut to the card's own proportion from the graded masters rather than reused from one of the four named placement crops, and the engagement with no assigned frame is handled deliberately rather than left as a hole.

Each speaker card proof is identifiable as the engagement it actually contains, verified from what is rendered inside it rather than from its position in the returned list, and the two sessions sharing an event name do not overwrite each other.

The AV monogram on every card is the recovered vector rather than the fuzzy baked artwork the supplied template carries, and nothing is claimed as press-ready with bleed that the supplied card file cannot carry, with the shortfall reported.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle what lands where: the pictures and the monogram on imaging, the three canvases on HTML authoring, and the speaker card run on the merge surface.
trajectory.judgement: Most of this reads as a crop exercise, and the temptation is to treat the whole thing that way. The actual structure is that four of the deliverables are defined by the ground or the size they have to survive, one is defined by being editable next month, and one is a genuine one-record-per-page run: a printed card per engagement off her roster, which is the merge surface and nothing else, and mistaking it for another authored canvas ships one card, not a run tied to her list.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface, the confirmed tier, and the card run marked as the merge job.

trajectory.action: Upload the nine frames, the card photograph and the workshop snap, holding a manifest with source dimensions.
trajectory.judgement: Source dimensions are recorded here because every no-invented-pixels claim later is made against them.
trajectory.produces: A manifest with source dimensions per file.

trajectory.action: Preview all nine and triage: which part of the afternoon each came from, how the grey behind her reads in each, how much room there is around her, and how her hair sits against the ground.
trajectory.judgement: The client has already picked her favourite as the press headshot, and the triage has to establish independently whether that frame can be brought to where the other eight are going. Accepting the client's hero without testing it against the set is the fast answer and it is the one that ends with eight frames matching each other and not the one she sends to organisers.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note and a stated view on the client's chosen hero.

trajectory.action: Fix one look on the strongest frame and correct the other eight toward it, one call per frame, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set. Frames from the two halves of the afternoon need different corrections to arrive at the same place, and a batched call applies one identical parameter set. The band rules out anything that reads as a preset signature.
trajectory.produces: Nine corrected masters with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked work where a whole-frame move is wrong: correct the ground or the sitter separately by naming the material rather than the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate, and skin and paper want opposite moves that cannot both be served globally.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the ground green or the skin warm.

trajectory.action: Produce the warm-neutral ground version in one operation where the frame allows it, and produce the ground-free version for the press kit and the deck.
trajectory.judgement: The one-call ground route and the select-invert-fill route are not interchangeable and the choice is per frame. The ground-free version has only one source of edge softness, and it is the same operation that produces the ground version, so the two are not independent decisions.
trajectory.produces: Warm-neutral and ground-free variants across the set.

trajectory.action: Place the ground-free versions on the deep ground her press kit and deck use and inspect the hair and shoulder edges close up.
trajectory.judgement: This is the only place the edge can be judged, because both failure modes are invisible on white and on the warm neutral. Deciding to look is the agent's own move; nothing prompts it.
trajectory.produces: An edge verdict per frame on the ground that matters.

trajectory.action: Compose the four crops for the four placements at the sizes each is actually used at, reading each crop's tradeoff metadata, and extend a frame at its edges rather than interpolating it where a placement needs more room than the frame holds.
trajectory.judgement: A profile picture and a banner are not the same crop scaled; the smallest placement needs the tightest composition and the widest needs room the studio frame does not have. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop interpolated, and adding edge material is the only route that does not.
trajectory.produces: Four composed crops per selected frame, with a resize and extension record.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, vector recovery
trajectory.action: Recover the monogram from the deboss card: a selection worded at what actually distinguishes the mark in this photograph, inverted for polarity, cropped to the selection's bounds, traced, then given a viewBox with the opaque ground path removed. Produce a solid variant for reversing.
trajectory.judgement: There is no ink to select, so the usual wording that takes a printed mark off a substrate has nothing to grip and the selection has to be aimed at what the photograph actually contains. Polarity decides whether the trace is a mark or a filled box, and background removal is the wrong instrument on letterforms with enclosed counters.
trajectory.produces: A transparent, scalable monogram plus a solid variant for the dark ground.

trajectory.action: Place the traced monogram at the profile picture's delivered size and reversed on the deep ground, and look at both.
trajectory.judgement: The two hardest placements she named are the two smallest and the two most reversed, and neither can be judged at canvas size. Looking at the mark at its real delivered size is a decision the agent has to make.
trajectory.produces: A verdict on the monogram at its two hardest placements.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a workshop or studio environmental frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward her look and lay it beside her graded frames.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose existing light can be brought to hers rather than the best thumbnail, and then judging whether it sits with her photography or reads as a stock picture behind her. A 240 pixel thumbnail is not evidence about light.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale environmental frame, graded and judged against the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read as a design studio founder at institutional level. Weight cannot be inferred from the style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug, and the CSS must use the returned stack.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes: the speaker one-pager at true physical dimensions, the wide banner and the square announcement. Embed every photograph as image data, place the monogram as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air the one-pager carries and how quietly the monogram sits at this band.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole set, uploaded and addressable, retained as a deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the other two, asserting per canvas that every photograph resolved to real image data, that the monogram arrived as vector shapes, and that nothing resolves past its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with three canvases, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the other two.

trajectory.action: Convert the print shop's speaker-card PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each holds, and whether a bleed box exists.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how the file was set. The three tidy fields may be one flowing story, the monogram that reads like a placed logo may be baked flat with no frame to bind into, and the one thing that is a real picture frame is the portrait well. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly rather than promised.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory, the bleed verdict, and a mapping strategy chosen from what the file actually contains.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the card's true story text from the interchange file, compute every field offset from that string, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export and confirm every expected placeholder is present, including the date that sits mid-story.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from whatever string it is handed, and preparation reports success either way, so a mapping read off the layout drops the mid-story date on every card and says nothing. The only evidence a field landed is finding its placeholder in the re-exported document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders, the date included, are confirmed by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Cut each engagement's card portrait from the graded masters to the card's own proportion, reading what each crop reports about its bounds and tradeoffs, and reconcile the crops against the roster including the engagement whose picture cell is blank.
trajectory.judgement: None of the four named placement crops is the card's proportion, so the card portraits are new cuts off the graded masters rather than a reuse, which is a return to imaging the template's shape forces. A blank picture cell is not an error the merge will raise, so what a card with no assigned portrait shows is decided here rather than found on the printed sheet.
trajectory.produces: A card portrait per engagement at the card proportion, with a stated treatment for the engagement that has none.

trajectory.action: Run the roster against the template binding each row's own portrait and carrying the recovered vector monogram, produce the printer's run and per-engagement proofs, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: One portrait repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, the naming key has to survive two sessions sharing an event name, and a file's position in the returned list is not evidence of which engagement is inside it. The monogram on the card has to be the recovered vector rather than the baked raster the template carried.
trajectory.produces: The speaker card run plus per-engagement proofs, each verified against its row.

trajectory.action: Create the board and add the finished set for her co-founder, treating a partial success as partial. Then write the note: per frame what was applied, any frame that could not be brought to the set, the type system, an honest statement of where the monogram holds and where it does not with what to use instead, and the speaker card run with its per-engagement identity check, the engagement that had no portrait, and the bleed reality of the supplied card file.
trajectory.judgement: The monogram note is the part she will actually rely on, and it has to say plainly what she cannot do with the artwork rather than leave her to find out on a conference programme. She asked for that note by name. The card run's shortfalls, the missing portrait and the missing bleed, are named here rather than shipped quietly.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover covering the pictures, the monogram, the canvases and the card run.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What a blind deboss actually yields as artwork, and whether it survives the two placements the client named as the ones she cares about. There is no ink and no colour in the mark: it exists only as the shadow the raking light threw into the paper relief, and only on the side the light came from, so what a selection returns is a property of that photograph's light rather than of the monogram. The trace comes back as a set of soft shadow shapes that read convincingly as the two letters at full canvas, which is the only size at which anyone would look at them by default, and which break into disconnected fragments with one side of each letterform missing at the size a profile picture reproduces them, and lose their remaining edge entirely when reversed on the deep ground. Nothing reports any of this. The tracing step takes no options at all, so there is no parameter to have set correctly; the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be chosen until the failure has been seen at real size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre-empt it. The trace's fidelity is a function of this photograph's raking light, the paper's texture and the selection that produced it. There is no measurement, no preview at delivered size, and no parameter on the trace. An agent that words the selection carefully and gets the polarity right still cannot know how much of each letterform survives without tracing it and putting it at avatar size. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the monogram is pressed into the paper with no ink and that it has to survive on a profile picture and reversed on the dark ground, which is the client naming her hardest placements and her standing requirement, exactly as she would to a designer. It does not say it will fail, and no asset note, earlier step or deliverable says which letter breaks or on which side. The client asking for a note about where it will and will not hold is a request for professional advice, not a disclosure that the answer is already known. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to go back and make a different asset: re-prepare the raster so the relief carries a usable edge before tracing, aim the selection at a different property of the photograph, or accept that the traced mark is a large-format asset only and build a different small-size lockup from the letterforms. Whichever it is, the one-pager, the banner and the announcement are then re-composed around a mark of a different weight and a different minimum size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster to strengthen the relief before tracing rather than trying to fix the trace, re-select on a wording aimed at what actually distinguishes the mark in this frame, re-trace, strip the ground path and inject a viewBox again, and re-place at profile-picture size and reversed on the deep ground rather than assuming the second attempt took. If it still will not hold at the smallest size, decide and state what carries that placement instead, and re-author the canvases around the mark's real minimum size, which changes the composition rather than just the asset.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A founder raising a seed round uses a profile picture on which her monogram is a smear of disconnected grey shapes, and sends conference organisers a press kit whose mark disappears entirely into the dark ground, having been handed artwork that looked perfect in every file she was shown.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the ground-free version actually holds where it is used. She has thick curly hair, the studio grey behind her sits close in value to it in the frames shot after the light was moved, and the knockout resolves that either by cutting hard into the curl or by leaving a soft rim of captured grey around it. Which of the two a given frame gets is a property of that frame's light and that part of her hair, not of the route chosen or the care taken, and both are completely invisible on white and on the warm neutral ground, which is exactly why every version she has tried herself looked fine until it went on her deck. The operation reports success in both cases and the returned file looks correct at normal viewing size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The ground-free version has to be made regardless of order, there is no metadata that reports edge quality, and no measurement is available. A careful agent choosing the right route still gets a rim or a hard cut on the frames where hair and ground share value, because the photograph is the variable. It also cannot be settled by inspecting the returned file in isolation: the failure only exists relative to the ground it is composited on. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says every version she has tried has a pale outline round her hair, which is the client describing the symptom that made her hire someone, not a description of which frames do it, why, or that the fix is ground-dependent. No asset note names the frames and no acceptance line explains the cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The fix is a different operation on a different principle, naming the paper behind her and inverting rather than asking for the subject, plus a decision about whether a frame whose curl cannot be cut cleanly stays in the set at all, which changes which frame carries which placement.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected frames by naming the ground material and inverting rather than by asking for the subject, re-composite on the deep ground and inspect the curl again rather than assuming the second route worked, and check the frames that were not flagged at the same close inspection, since the reason to look was found on one frame and the rest have not been established as clean. If a frame will not cut cleanly at all, move the placement it was carrying to a frame that will and say so.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Her press kit and her investor deck both carry a portrait with a pale halo traced round every curl on a very dark ground, which is the precise defect she hired someone to fix, shipped back to her as fixed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed environmental frame can sit with her own portraits. Stock search returns a small CDN thumbnail; the frame's true light, its true neutral and its true black point only exist after it is licensed, downloaded at full resolution and brought toward her look, and whether it then reads as her studio or as a stock picture placed behind her is only visible with it and her nine graded frames laid out together. Two candidate frames that look equally warm and equally quiet at thumbnail size can be a full grade apart at full resolution, and one of them will never join a set built on a studio portrait's soft key.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The comparison needs both the licensed frame and the finished set to exist, so it cannot be moved earlier, and it cannot be settled by care, because a thumbnail is not evidence about light. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the banner wants more room than a studio frame and that she will pay for one if that is what it needs, which is an invitation carrying no claim about how a candidate will behave. No asset, no acceptance line and no earlier step names it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The likely response is to abandon the licensed frame and search again on different terms, which is a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement, not the same operation on changed input, and it may instead resolve into extending one of her own frames at the edges and accepting a tighter banner, which changes the banner's composition and the type that sits on it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame further toward her look, or, if it will not join, return to Stock with a search framed by the light her set actually has rather than by the subject matter, license a replacement and re-grade it, then lay the set out again and judge it as ten rather than checking the new frame alone. If nothing joins, extend one of her own frames at its edges instead and re-compose the banner around the room that produces, which is a different banner.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The banner at the top of a founder's profile reads as a bought photograph with a portrait pasted on it, in front of the investors and programme committees the whole kit exists to persuade.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered speaker card actually contains the engagement its filename claims. The natural way to hand a founder a proof per talk is a multi-record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and returns a list labelled by row number. The labels do not match: the files come back in an order that does not follow the roster, and nothing in the response says so. Every gate above it passes, the page count equals the row count, each file is a valid card, and the only way to find out is to open the cards and read the event, the date and the talk title inside them against the row they were named for. The two sessions that share an event name compound it, because a key built on the event name alone overwrites one card with the other before the order problem is even reached.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mislabelling is in the response itself, and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name the files. It cannot be pre-empted by care, because the run reports success and the returned list looks authoritative. (b) Nothing states it. The acceptance line that each card must carry its own talk is the client's requirement, and the brief never characterises how the run is delivered or that the raster route reverses. No asset note and no earlier step names it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different delivery route, a single multi-page render whose page order is trustworthy or a per-record loop producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed, plus a naming key that survives two sessions sharing an event name, which is a new route and a new key rather than the same call on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi-record raster route, re-run the card set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually rendered inside it rather than from its position in the list, and re-check the two sessions that share an event name so the collision does not silently overwrite one with the other. If a card's cut portrait does not hold at the card's real printed size, return to imaging and re-cut it before the run is trusted.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A founder emails a conference organiser a speaker card whose talk title and date belong to a different conference, and hands out at a fireside a card carrying the panel's session instead, printed and sitting in delegate packs, discovered by the organisers she is asking for stage time rather than by her.

deliverables.name: Vellacourt session set, nine frames at one look
deliverables.spec: Nine frames from a shifting afternoon brought to one composed, credible, understated look with no visible retouching signature and the sitter still recognisably herself, delivered at the four placement crops composed for the size each is actually used at rather than scaled from one master, every output at or below its source dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log and every resize or edge extension any tool reported. One set with one look, not nine separately optimised pictures and not one picture at four sizes.

deliverables.name: Warm-neutral and ground-free portrait variants
deliverables.spec: Each selected frame delivered on the warm neutral ground the client asked for, replacing the studio grey, and as a ground-free version whose edge holds on the deep ground her press kit and investor deck use, with no pale rim and no hard-cut curl, judged on that ground rather than on white. Where a frame cannot be cut cleanly, it is named and the placement it was carrying is moved.

deliverables.name: Recovered AV monogram
deliverables.spec: The monogram recovered from a photograph of a blind-debossed card as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque full-canvas ground path, delivered as a transparent mark and a solid variant for reversing, together with an honest written statement of where it holds and where it does not, specifically at profile-picture size and reversed on the deep ground, and what to use instead wherever it does not.

deliverables.name: Speaker one-pager, banner and announcement as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable Express document carrying a speaker one-pager at true physical dimensions, a wide banner canvas and a square announcement canvas, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the monogram as real vector shapes and every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, since the event name and date change every time.

deliverables.name: Per-engagement speaker card run
deliverables.spec: The print shop's flat single-record card PDF reverse-engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder, the mid-story date included, confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the season roster: the printer's run with page count equal to the engagement count, each card carrying its own talk's title, event and date and its own portrait cut to the card proportion from the graded masters, the recovered vector monogram in place of the template's baked raster, plus per-engagement proofs named from what is actually rendered inside them on a key that survives two sessions sharing an event name, with the engagement that has no portrait handled deliberately and the supplied file's lack of bleed reported rather than claimed away.

deliverables.name: Handover note and review board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per frame what was applied, any frame that could not be brought to the set and why, the type system by role with foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the honest account of the monogram's limits and the alternative for the placements it cannot carry, whether anything was licensed and why, and every resize or edge extension any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the finished set for her co-founder to sign off, with nothing silently dropped.

Both strings must be present.

decision_gates: Whether the client's chosen press frame can be brought to where the other eight are going, and what to say if it cannot.
How far each half of the afternoon is pushed to reach one look, and where a correction stops being a correction and becomes a preset signature.
Knockout route per frame rather than per set, and on which ground the edges are judged, given that both failure modes are invisible on white.
Whether a frame whose curl will not cut cleanly stays in the set, and which placement moves if it does not.
Composing four crops for four delivered sizes rather than deriving them from one master, and which frame carries which placement.
Whether to extend a frame at its edges or accept a tighter banner, knowing extended material has to match her own ground.
How to word a selection on a mark that has no ink and no colour, where the usual wording for lifting a printed mark off a substrate has nothing to grip.
Which raster preparation gives the relief a usable edge before tracing, given that the tracing step takes no options at all.
Whether the traced mark is a large-format asset only, and if so what carries the small placements instead.
Whether the licensed environmental frame joins her photography or reads as bought, and if bought, whether to push it, search again on the light, or abandon it for an extended frame of her own.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an institutional founder rather than a personal brand.
How much air the one-pager carries and how quietly the monogram sits. At this band restraint is the design.
What to escalate in writing versus what to fix silently, on a commission where the client explicitly asked to be told where her own mark will not work.

Which delivery route carries per-engagement identity safely for the speaker card run, given the multi-record raster proof route returns in an order its own response mislabels, and what key names a card file when two sessions share an event name.

Which portrait crop carries which engagement's card, cut to the card's own proportion from the graded masters rather than reused from a named placement crop, and what a card for a just-confirmed engagement with no assigned portrait shows.

Whether the card's monogram is the recovered vector carried as a shared element or the template's baked raster, and whether a press-ready-with-bleed run can be honoured from a card file whose media box equals its trim.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a portrait of somebody who is not her. IDENTITY is the entire commission: these are nine frames of one specific person who is about to ask investors for money and conference committees for stage time, and her monogram is a specific impression in a specific piece of paper from a printer that has closed. A regenerated face is fraud and a regenerated monogram is a different studio's mark. SPEC: she needs four crops composed for four named delivered sizes, a version on a warm neutral ground and a version with genuine transparency whose edge holds on a dark ground, all at or below source resolution. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked. EDITABILITY: one deliverable is defined by being editable, three canvases in one document she changes per event so she is not paying for this four times, with live text and real vector geometry. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this hair cut cleanly on the ground it will actually sit on, does this shadow trace still read at avatar size, does this licensed frame sit with her portraits. None of that is a generation problem, and the honest note about where her mark will not hold is professional advice a render cannot give. And the speaker card run is a genuine one-record-per-page job: one printed card per engagement, each bound to its own talk's title, event and date and its own portrait, page count equal to the roster, with the mid-story date landing on every card and each proof carrying the engagement it claims. A model returns a picture of a card, not a run of them tied to a roster and checkable row by row, and cannot tell her that the file its print shop supplied carries no bleed.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted and deliberately not padded: the InDesign surface is invoked for the one genuine variable-data run this commission actually contains, the per-engagement speaker card run off her season roster, while the Illustrator tools are still never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host. Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: masked and unmasked image_apply_adjustments, auto_tone, select_by_prompt and select_subject with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and the backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, generative_expand and vectorize are all verified headless across the audit's live calls. The one-call solid-ground knockout is verified and is the correct route for the warm neutral; transparent RGBA with genuinely feathered partial alpha is verified and survives both crop tools at png output, which is what the ground-free deliverable depends on, and the documented note that outputFileType must stay png through the whole chain is why a single jpeg step would destroy it. remove_background is documented as failing on disjoint marks and enclosed interiors, which is why the monogram is recovered by selection, inversion and tracing rather than by background removal. vectorize takes no options at all, emits no viewBox and always emits an opaque first path, all verified, so the hygiene the deliverable gates on is real work the agent must do itself. The prompt-wording asymmetry, where naming the substrate returns the substrate and naming the mark's own visual properties returns the mark, is a verified live finding, and a blind deboss is precisely the case where the mark has no colour or medium of its own to name, which is what makes the preparation the only lever. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard cap and reporting it only in tradeoffs, and remove_background is documented as silently downscaling oversized inputs and reporting it only as a tradeoff, so the no-invented-pixels bar is scored as a decision plus a disclosure rather than as any measurement the agent takes. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and a prefixed picture column, and document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page for a PDF-derived template and page count equal to row count. The story-offset finding is leaned on directly: a mapping validated on offsets read off the layout drops the mid-story date while preparation reports success either way, so the date placeholder is confirmed only by inspecting the re-exported interchange file. The proof-identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi-record PNG and JPEG output comes back REVERSED while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes. PDF-derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and no bleed can be introduced into a file whose media box equals its trim, so the bleed shortfall is scored as a disclosure rather than a delivery, and the card portraits are cut in imaging because the template exposes one real picture frame and the monogram baked flat, so the recovered vector rides as a shared element rather than a bound field. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, true physical canvases resolve exactly at absolute units, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, external image URLs render as empty placeholders so every photograph is embedded as image data, and the right-anchored auto-sized wrapper failure is a verified live finding the trajectory designs against. Transport goes through the text/html upload path because embedded photography exceeds the inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the editable document plus the self-contained source. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified end to end in a real browser, and the non-standard numeric weights, the display-cut-by-slug rule, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are all live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only because long queries return zero hits, the orientation filter is broken and never passed, licensing returns genuine camera-scale imagery, and boards persist with a twelve-placement cap where 201 means partial success with a failed-items list. VOLUME: eleven client image files plus a flat card template PDF and an eight-row roster CSV in, roughly forty image artefacts moved in total including the eight card-proportion portraits and the eight per-engagement card proofs, every multi-image call at or under the ten-item cap, the merge run at eight records, and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no AI object removal, no from-scratch image generation, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.
